# YOUR JOB — Sprint S24: AI Assist schema (4 migrations)

S24 is Epic 2 scaffolding. Zero AI job implementations here — just tables, RLS, indexes. The 3 actual AI jobs are S25/S26/S27.

## Context

Existing infra:
- `ai_design_requests` + `ai_design_outputs` tables exist (Sprint 9 — design assistant)
- `conversations` table with `channel` CHECK ('sms','email','instagram','facebook','voice') — missing `whatsapp` + `webchat`
- `client_communications` table (message rows, child of conversations)
- `lib/ai/budget.ts` — `requireAiBudget(supabase, studioId, estimatedCostCents)` checks daily cap via `ai_design_outputs` sum — S24 will add a proper `ai_costs` table

## Migration 1: `20260514100000_ai_assist_schema.sql`

Four tables in one migration (they're tightly coupled):

### Table A: `ai_jobs`
Tracks every AI Assist job request.

```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS public.ai_jobs (
  id                uuid        PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  studio_id         uuid        NOT NULL REFERENCES public.studios(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  artist_id         uuid        REFERENCES public.artists(id) ON DELETE SET NULL, -- optional: which artist triggered
  job_type          text        NOT NULL CHECK (job_type IN ('reply_draft','consult_summary','aftercare_gen')),
  status            text        NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending' CHECK (status IN ('pending','processing','done','failed','cancelled')),
  model             text        NOT NULL DEFAULT 'claude-sonnet-4-6',
  input_tokens      integer,
  output_tokens     integer,
  cost_cents        integer     NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (cost_cents >= 0),
  input_context     jsonb       NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,   -- job-specific params (conversation_id, session_id, etc.)
  output            jsonb,                                       -- raw model output before human review
  error             text,                                        -- set on failure
  triggered_by      uuid        REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  created_at        timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  started_at        timestamptz,
  completed_at      timestamptz
);
```

Indexes: `(studio_id, created_at DESC)`, `(studio_id, job_type)`, `(status)` WHERE status IN ('pending','processing'), `(artist_id)` WHERE artist_id IS NOT NULL.

RLS: Studio members (owner/admin/artist) SELECT + INSERT their own studio's jobs. No UPDATE/DELETE from app — status transitions via service-role only (BullMQ workers). `CREATE POLICY ... USING (studio_id IN (SELECT studio_id FROM studio_members WHERE user_id = auth.uid()))`.

### Table B: `ai_costs`
Per-job cost ledger for billing reconciliation and budget enforcement.

```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS public.ai_costs (
  id          uuid        PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  studio_id   uuid        NOT NULL REFERENCES public.studios(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  job_id      uuid        REFERENCES public.ai_jobs(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  job_type    text        NOT NULL,                              -- denorm from job for aggregation without join
  model       text        NOT NULL,
  input_tokens  integer   NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  output_tokens integer   NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  cost_cents    integer   NOT NULL CHECK (cost_cents >= 0),
  created_at  timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
```

Indexes: `(studio_id, created_at DESC)` for budget queries, `(studio_id, job_type, created_at)` for per-type analytics, `(job_id)`.

RLS: SELECT for studio members (owner/admin). INSERT by service_role only (workers write this after job completion). No UPDATE/DELETE.

### Table C: `ai_voice_profiles`
Per-studio (and optionally per-artist) trained tone profile.

```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS public.ai_voice_profiles (
  id                uuid        PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  studio_id         uuid        NOT NULL REFERENCES public.studios(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  artist_id         uuid        REFERENCES public.artists(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, -- NULL = studio-level profile
  tone_fingerprint  jsonb       NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,   -- {adjectives: [], phrases: [], avoid: [], examples: []}
  message_count     integer     NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,             -- how many messages were used to train
  last_rebuilt_at   timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  created_at        timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at        timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  UNIQUE (studio_id, artist_id)   -- one profile per studio OR per studio+artist combo
);
```

Indexes: `(studio_id)`, `(studio_id, artist_id)`.

RLS: SELECT for studio members. INSERT/UPDATE by service_role (nightly cron rebuilds). No DELETE from app.

`updated_at` trigger: use `set_updated_at()` (existing).

### Table D: `ai_drafts`
One row per AI-drafted message candidate awaiting human approval.

```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS public.ai_drafts (
  id               uuid        PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  studio_id        uuid        NOT NULL REFERENCES public.studios(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  conversation_id  uuid        REFERENCES public.conversations(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, -- nullable: consult_summary has no convo
  job_id           uuid        NOT NULL REFERENCES public.ai_jobs(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  draft_type       text        NOT NULL CHECK (draft_type IN ('reply','consult_summary','aftercare')),
  body             text        NOT NULL,                        -- the AI-generated text
  status           text        NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending' CHECK (status IN ('pending','approved','discarded','sent')),
  approved_by      uuid        REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  approved_at      timestamptz,
  sent_at          timestamptz,
  created_at       timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

-- INVARIANT (enforced at application layer + tested in Luna):
-- status='sent' is ONLY reachable if status='approved' first.
-- No autonomous sending. Every draft must pass human approval.
COMMENT ON TABLE public.ai_drafts IS
  'AI-generated message drafts awaiting human approval. '
  'Never transitions directly to sent without approved intermediate state. '
  'application_level_invariant: APPROVED before SENT — tested in Luna.';
```

Indexes: `(studio_id, created_at DESC)`, `(conversation_id)` WHERE conversation_id IS NOT NULL, `(job_id)`, `(status)` WHERE status = 'pending'.

RLS: Studio members (owner/admin/artist) SELECT their studio's drafts. `UPDATE` allowed for status transitions (approve/discard) by owner/admin/artist. INSERT service_role only (worker writes draft). No DELETE.

## Migration 2: `20260514100100_conversations_channel_extend.sql`

Extend `conversations.channel` CHECK constraint to include `whatsapp` and `webchat`.

```sql
-- Extend channel CHECK to cover all current webhook sources
ALTER TABLE public.conversations
  DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS conversations_channel_check;

ALTER TABLE public.conversations
  ADD CONSTRAINT conversations_channel_check
    CHECK (channel IN ('sms','email','instagram','whatsapp','facebook','voice','webchat'));
```

Also add `whatsapp` and `webchat` to the COMMENT.

## Migration 3: `20260514100200_ai_jobs_budget_rpc.sql`

RPC `get_studio_ai_budget_usage(p_studio_id uuid, p_days int DEFAULT 1)` — returns current spend + cap:

```sql
RETURNS jsonb
-- Returns: { total_cost_cents: bigint, cap_cents: bigint, budget_remaining_cents: bigint, days: int, job_count: int }
-- cap = 500 cents ($5/day) per day × p_days
-- Query: SUM(cost_cents) FROM ai_costs WHERE studio_id=p_studio_id AND created_at >= now()-p_days
-- Also: count of jobs in that window
```

SECURITY DEFINER, `SET search_path = public`, GRANT authenticated (studio members can see their own budget state).

Also add RPC `record_ai_cost(p_studio_id uuid, p_job_id uuid, p_job_type text, p_model text, p_input_tokens int, p_output_tokens int, p_cost_cents int)` — called by workers after job completion. REVOKE from authenticated, GRANT to service_role only.

## Critical rules

1. Every table: RLS enabled, rollback comment, `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`.
2. No `numeric`/`float` — always `integer` cents.
3. `set_updated_at()` trigger on `ai_voice_profiles`.
4. CC48 check: RPC return key names must match the TS contract Koda will write in `lib/ai/contracts.ts`.
5. After writing, run:
   ```bash
   cd "/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/InkOS"
   supabase db push
   supabase gen types typescript --project-id lagxpynhhjhcclzciznb --schema public > lib/supabase/types.ts
   # Strip CLI version notice from end of file if present
   pnpm typecheck
   ```
6. Push must succeed clean. If any constraint violation, fix and retry.

## Deliverables

1. 3 migration file paths
2. `supabase db push` succeeded (confirm)
3. `pnpm typecheck` zero new errors
4. RPC signatures for Koda (exact function names + param names + return JSON keys)
5. Any schema surprises

Caveman. No fluff.

1	---
2	name: InkOS Build Lessons
3	description: Lessons extracted from the InkOS 13-sprint tattoo studio SaaS build (2026-04-15 to 2026-04-16). Stack A (Next 16 + Supabase + Dodo + Railway). 644 files, 18 migrations, 140 routes. Every pattern here feeds all future Boldteq builds.
4	type: project
5	priority: high
6	source: InkOS, 2026-04-16
7	usage_metric: 0
8	knowledge_version: v1
9	---
10	
11	# InkOS Build Lessons
12	
13	## 1. Recurring Sage Findings — Systematic Pipeline Weaknesses
14	
15	### 1A. RPC Parameter Mismatches (Dato writes RPC, Koda writes route with different params)
16	
17	Appeared in Sprint 5 (C1: camelCase `submissionId` vs snake_case `submission_id` in consent PDF job), Sprint 6 (C1: `public_get_invite_by_token` vs `get_invite_by_token`; C2: `accept_team_invite` missing `artist_id` and `commission_default_pct` in return shape), Sprint 7 (M1: `applied_date` vs `applied_at`), and Sprint 8 (S8#1: `set_artist_tax_info` param mismatch). Root cause: Dato writes the migration defining the RPC signature, Koda writes the API route consuming it, and neither verifies the other's contract. The hand-written `lib/supabase/types.ts` masks the drift because TypeScript trusts whatever is manually typed. **Prevention rule:** Before Koda writes any route that calls an RPC, the RPC's exact parameter names and return fields must be extracted from the migration SQL into a shared TypeScript interface. If Dato and Koda run in parallel, the contract must be defined in the design spec as a shared interface BEFORE either starts coding.
18	
19	### 1B. Column Name Drift (migration says X, types say Y, code says Z)
20	
21	Appeared in Sprint 1 (C3: `locations` migration missing `zip`/`phone` that types declared), Sprint 3 (C2: `sort_order` column missing from migration but code referenced it), Sprint 6 (C3: `studio_members.last_active_at` not in migration but in types), Sprint 7 (M1: `applied_date` vs `applied_at`), Sprint 8-12 audit (S11#8: `status` column on `marketing_campaigns` missing, S12#12: `payroll_items` table referenced but doesn't exist). Root cause: `lib/supabase/types.ts` was hand-edited throughout the build instead of regenerated from the actual DB schema. **Prevention rule:** Never hand-edit the types file. After every Dato migration, run `pnpm supabase gen types typescript --linked > lib/supabase/types.ts`. If the Supabase project doesn't exist yet (as in InkOS), maintain a strict convention: Dato writes the migration, Dato updates types to exactly match, and Koda does NOT touch the types file. Any column referenced in code must exist in the migration first.
22	
23	### 1C. `asChild` Violations on base-nova
24	
25	Every Sage audit checked for `asChild` usage on base-nova (shadcn/ui's `@base-ui-components/react`) components. In InkOS this passed cleanly because it was caught early (Sprint 1 scan), but the automated grep for `asChild` was added to every single audit because this is a known recurring problem across Boldteq builds. **Rule:** All components from base-nova use the `render` prop pattern, never `asChild`. This must be in every project's ESLint config as a custom rule or at minimum in the Sage automated scan.
26	
27	### 1D. Missing Rate Limits on GET Endpoints
28	
29	Sprint 1 (M1: auth rate limits architecturally impossible), Sprint 6 (public invite route needed rate limit), Sprint 8-12 combined audit (cross-sprint #17: payroll GET routes missing rate limits). Koda consistently forgets rate limits on read routes, treating them as "safe." But unbounded GETs enable enumeration, scraping, and DoS. **Rule:** Every API route, GET or POST, must import and call either `authedRatelimit` or `publicBookingReadRatelimit` before any DB query. Sage scans for routes missing rate-limit calls.
30	
31	### 1E. `onValueChange` Null Guards for base-ui Select
32	
33	Not specific to InkOS (passed here) but flagged as a check item in every audit. When base-ui Select fires `onValueChange`, the value can be `null` on deselect. Without a guard, the handler crashes or sends null to the API. **Rule:** Every `onValueChange` handler must check `if (value === null) return` before processing.
34	
35	### 1F. `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` Violations
36	
37	Sprint 4 build report (item #2): interface optionals needed `| undefined` suffix. Throughout the build, Koda hit TypeScript errors where `{ field?: string }` doesn't accept `undefined` under strict optional property types. **Rule:** Under `exactOptionalPropertyTypes: true`, always declare optional fields as `field?: string | undefined` in interfaces. Or better: use Zod schema inference (`z.infer<typeof Schema>`) which handles this automatically.
38	
39	### 1G. Feature Gate Key Mismatches
40	
41	Sprint 7 (C1): the plans JSONB in the billing migration used `commission_splits` but all code used `commissions`. Today's static `requireFeature()` compares plan order (not JSONB keys), so it accidentally worked. But if anyone switches to the RPC-based `requireFeatureRpc()` (which reads JSONB), all gates 403. **Rule:** Define all feature gate keys in a single `lib/billing/feature-keys.ts` constant. Both the migration seed data and the `requireFeature()` callers import from this file. Drift is a compile error instead of a runtime surprise.
42	
43	### 1H. Public Routes Using Session Client Instead of Anon
44	
45	Sprint 5 (C6, C7): public consent pages imported `createClient` from `@/lib/supabase/server` (session-cookie client) instead of `createPublicClient`. Functional today (RPC grants to anon) but leaks the logged-in user's session into a public route. **Rule:** Every route under `/book/`, `/consent/`, `/invite/`, or `/api/public/` must use `createPublicClient()` from `@/lib/supabase/public`. Sage grepping for `createClient` in public routes is now a mandatory scan.
46	
47	### 1I. `unstable_cache` Capturing Authenticated Clients
48	
49	Sprint 7 (M3): `unstable_cache(async () => supabase.rpc(...))` captured the first caller's authenticated client. Subsequent requests within the cache TTL reuse the first caller's JWT. **Rule:** Never wrap `supabase.rpc()` calls in `unstable_cache` when the supabase client is session-scoped. Cache the RESULT of the RPC call (a plain object), not the client invocation. Or just don't use `unstable_cache` for authenticated data -- it's not worth the footgun.
50	
51	## 2. Sprint Velocity Patterns — What Worked for Parallel Execution
52	
53	### 2A. Dato + Vega in Parallel (No Dependency)
54	
55	Dato writes the migration (schema, RPCs, RLS, triggers) while Vega writes the design spec (UI layout, component hierarchy, interaction patterns). These have zero dependencies. Starting them in parallel saves 2-4 hours per sprint. Koda then consumes BOTH outputs to build the API routes and UI.
56	
57	### 2B. Sage Audit in Background While Next Sprint Starts
58	
59	After Koda delivers a sprint, Sage audits the output while Dato and Vega start on the next sprint. The next sprint's Koda build can begin on features that don't overlap with the audit scope. This pipeline parallelism was critical for shipping 13 sprints in 2 days. Exception: if Sage's audit is BLOCK severity, the fix Koda must run before proceeding.
60	
61	### 2C. Fix Koda + Build Koda Can Run in Parallel If File Scopes Don't Overlap
62	
63	When Sage flags fixes in Sprint N, a "fix Koda" agent addresses those while a "build Koda" agent starts Sprint N+1's non-overlapping files. This worked well when Sprint 3 fixes (client CRM) ran alongside Sprint 4 scaffold (billing). Does NOT work when the fix touches shared infrastructure like `lib/supabase/types.ts` or `lib/supabase/server.ts`.
64	
65	### 2D. API 500 Errors Recovered by Checking Partial State
66	
67	When a sprint's build partially failed (e.g., missing column caused a 500), Yash dispatched a fix agent that first checked what was already built and correct, then surgically fixed only the broken parts. Avoids the temptation to rewrite entire files.
68	
69	### 2E. Batch Sage Audits Are Worse Than Per-Sprint Audits
70	
71	Sprints 8-12 were batched into one combined Sage audit. This found 4 critical issues that had been compounding for 5 sprints. Per-sprint audits (Sprints 1-7) caught issues immediately, before they could cascade. **Rule:** Run Sage after EVERY sprint, not batched. The 30-minute audit cost per sprint is cheaper than the 4-hour compound fix session.
72	
73	## 3. Architecture Decisions That Proved Right
74	
75	### 3A. RPC-Only Writes for Audit-Critical Tables
76	
77	`consent_form_submissions` has zero direct-write RLS policies -- all writes go through `submit_consent_form` RPC. `commission_records` same pattern. This means: (a) business logic (snapshot creation, audit hash, penalty generation) can't be bypassed; (b) the RPC is the single source of truth for mutation semantics; (c) RLS stays simple (just read policies). **Apply to:** Any table where data integrity is a legal or financial obligation (consent, pay, billing, audit logs).
78	
79	### 3B. `EXCLUDE USING gist` for Booking Conflicts
80	
81	The `bookings_artist_no_overlap` exclusion constraint catches double-bookings at the DB level. Every write path (API route, public RPC, admin override) that creates/moves a booking is automatically protected. Without this, every write path would need its own conflict-check query, and one would inevitably be missed. Effort to set up: 5 lines of SQL. Effort saved: hours of bug-hunting. **Apply to:** Any domain with time-range conflicts (schedules, reservations, resource allocation).
82	
83	### 3C. `GENERATED ALWAYS` Columns for Computed Values
84	
85	`bookings.end_at` is `GENERATED ALWAYS AS (scheduled_at + (duration_min || ' minutes')::interval) STORED`. This means `end_at` can never drift from `scheduled_at + duration`. No code path can accidentally set a wrong `end_at`. Sage verified this by grepping for `end_at` in INSERT/UPDATE payloads -- zero hits. **Apply to:** Any column that's a deterministic function of other columns (totals, dates, durations).
86	
87	### 3D. Feature Gate Server-Enforced + UI-Hidden (Dual Enforcement)
88	
89	Every gated feature has: (1) `requireFeature(plan, 'key')` in the API route that returns 403, AND (2) `featureKey` in the sidebar nav-config that hides the link AND (3) `<UpgradeGate>` component that shows a blur overlay. Three layers means a user can never reach a paid feature through URL manipulation, deep linking, or API probing. **Apply to:** Every SaaS with tiered plans.
90	
91	### 3E. Worker-Only for Expensive Operations
92	
93	AI design generation (Claude + DALL-E pipeline), PDF generation (react-pdf/renderer), and low-stock email alerts all run in BullMQ workers, never in API routes. This prevents: request timeouts, memory pressure on the web process, and blocking other requests. **Apply to:** Any operation that takes >5s or uses >100MB memory.
94	
95	## 4. Architecture Decisions That Caused Problems
96	
97	### 4A. Hand-Written `lib/supabase/types.ts`
98	
99	This was the single largest source of bugs across the entire build. Every sprint had at least one finding traceable to types not matching the migration. The types file was 3000+ lines of manually maintained TypeScript that drifted from reality. **Fix for future builds:** Use `pnpm supabase gen types typescript` after every migration. If the Supabase project doesn't exist yet, use `supabase start` locally and generate from the local DB. Never hand-edit.
100

-- ============================================================
-- Migration: 20260514100000_ai_assist_schema
-- Purpose  : S24 Epic 2 scaffold — four AI Assist tables.
--            Zero AI job implementations here; tables only.
--            Tables: ai_jobs, ai_costs, ai_voice_profiles, ai_drafts
-- Rollback :
--   DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS set_ai_voice_profiles_updated_at ON ai_voice_profiles;
--   DROP TABLE IF EXISTS ai_drafts;
--   DROP TABLE IF EXISTS ai_voice_profiles;
--   DROP TABLE IF EXISTS ai_costs;
--   DROP TABLE IF EXISTS ai_jobs;
-- ============================================================

-- ============================================================
-- A. ai_jobs
-- Tracks every AI Assist job request. Status transitions are
-- service-role-only (BullMQ workers). App code may SELECT/INSERT.
-- ============================================================

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS public.ai_jobs (
  id             uuid        PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  studio_id      uuid        NOT NULL REFERENCES public.studios(id)  ON DELETE CASCADE,
  artist_id      uuid                 REFERENCES public.artists(id)  ON DELETE SET NULL,
  job_type       text        NOT NULL
                   CHECK (job_type IN ('reply_draft', 'consult_summary', 'aftercare_gen')),
  status         text        NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending'
                   CHECK (status IN ('pending', 'processing', 'done', 'failed', 'cancelled')),
  model          text        NOT NULL DEFAULT 'claude-sonnet-4-6',
  input_tokens   integer,
  output_tokens  integer,
  cost_cents     integer     NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (cost_cents >= 0),
  input_context  jsonb       NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  output         jsonb,
  error          text,
  triggered_by   uuid                 REFERENCES auth.users(id)      ON DELETE SET NULL,
  created_at     timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  started_at     timestamptz,
  completed_at   timestamptz
);

ALTER TABLE public.ai_jobs ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

-- Studio members (any role) can read their studio's jobs
CREATE POLICY ai_jobs_select
  ON public.ai_jobs
  FOR SELECT
  USING (
    studio_id IN (
      SELECT sm.studio_id FROM public.studio_members sm
      WHERE sm.user_id = auth.uid()
    )
  );

-- Studio members (owner/admin/artist) can insert jobs (trigger new AI work)
CREATE POLICY ai_jobs_insert
  ON public.ai_jobs
  FOR INSERT
  WITH CHECK (
    studio_id IN (
      SELECT sm.studio_id FROM public.studio_members sm
      WHERE sm.user_id = auth.uid()
        AND sm.role IN ('owner', 'admin', 'artist')
    )
  );

-- No UPDATE/DELETE from app — workers use service_role

-- Indexes
CREATE INDEX idx_ai_jobs_studio_created
  ON public.ai_jobs (studio_id, created_at DESC);

CREATE INDEX idx_ai_jobs_studio_type
  ON public.ai_jobs (studio_id, job_type);

CREATE INDEX idx_ai_jobs_status_active
  ON public.ai_jobs (status)
  WHERE status IN ('pending', 'processing');

CREATE INDEX idx_ai_jobs_artist
  ON public.ai_jobs (artist_id)
  WHERE artist_id IS NOT NULL;

-- ============================================================
-- B. ai_costs
-- Per-job cost ledger for billing reconciliation and budget
-- enforcement. Inserted by workers (service_role) after job
-- completion. App reads for budget display.
-- ============================================================

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS public.ai_costs (
  id             uuid        PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  studio_id      uuid        NOT NULL REFERENCES public.studios(id)  ON DELETE CASCADE,
  job_id         uuid                 REFERENCES public.ai_jobs(id)  ON DELETE SET NULL,
  job_type       text        NOT NULL,
  model          text        NOT NULL,
  input_tokens   integer     NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  output_tokens  integer     NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  cost_cents     integer     NOT NULL CHECK (cost_cents >= 0),
  created_at     timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

ALTER TABLE public.ai_costs ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

-- Owner/admin can read cost records for their studio
CREATE POLICY ai_costs_select
  ON public.ai_costs
  FOR SELECT
  USING (
    studio_id IN (
      SELECT sm.studio_id FROM public.studio_members sm
      WHERE sm.user_id = auth.uid()
        AND sm.role IN ('owner', 'admin')
    )
  );

-- INSERT by service_role only (workers) — no authenticated INSERT policy

-- Indexes
CREATE INDEX idx_ai_costs_studio_created
  ON public.ai_costs (studio_id, created_at DESC);

CREATE INDEX idx_ai_costs_studio_type_created
  ON public.ai_costs (studio_id, job_type, created_at);

CREATE INDEX idx_ai_costs_job
  ON public.ai_costs (job_id);

-- ============================================================
-- C. ai_voice_profiles
-- Per-studio (or per-studio+artist) trained tone fingerprint.
-- Rebuilt by nightly cron (service_role). App reads for prompt
-- construction. UNIQUE(studio_id, artist_id) with NULL artist_id
-- = studio-level profile.
-- ============================================================

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS public.ai_voice_profiles (
  id               uuid        PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  studio_id        uuid        NOT NULL REFERENCES public.studios(id)  ON DELETE CASCADE,
  artist_id        uuid                 REFERENCES public.artists(id)  ON DELETE CASCADE,
  tone_fingerprint jsonb       NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  message_count    integer     NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  last_rebuilt_at  timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  created_at       timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at       timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  UNIQUE NULLS NOT DISTINCT (studio_id, artist_id)
);

ALTER TABLE public.ai_voice_profiles ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

-- Studio members can read voice profiles
CREATE POLICY ai_voice_profiles_select
  ON public.ai_voice_profiles
  FOR SELECT
  USING (
    studio_id IN (
      SELECT sm.studio_id FROM public.studio_members sm
      WHERE sm.user_id = auth.uid()
    )
  );

-- INSERT/UPDATE by service_role only (nightly cron rebuilds)

-- Indexes
CREATE INDEX idx_ai_voice_profiles_studio
  ON public.ai_voice_profiles (studio_id);

CREATE INDEX idx_ai_voice_profiles_studio_artist
  ON public.ai_voice_profiles (studio_id, artist_id);

-- updated_at trigger
CREATE TRIGGER set_ai_voice_profiles_updated_at
  BEFORE UPDATE ON public.ai_voice_profiles
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION set_updated_at();

-- ============================================================
-- D. ai_drafts
-- AI-generated message candidates awaiting human approval.
-- INVARIANT: status='sent' is only reachable after status='approved'.
-- No autonomous sending. Workers INSERT; app UPDATEs status.
-- ============================================================

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS public.ai_drafts (
  id               uuid        PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  studio_id        uuid        NOT NULL REFERENCES public.studios(id)       ON DELETE CASCADE,
  conversation_id  uuid                 REFERENCES public.conversations(id)  ON DELETE CASCADE,
  job_id           uuid        NOT NULL REFERENCES public.ai_jobs(id)        ON DELETE CASCADE,
  draft_type       text        NOT NULL
                     CHECK (draft_type IN ('reply', 'consult_summary', 'aftercare')),
  body             text        NOT NULL,
  status           text        NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending'
                     CHECK (status IN ('pending', 'approved', 'discarded', 'sent')),
  approved_by      uuid                 REFERENCES auth.users(id)            ON DELETE SET NULL,
  approved_at      timestamptz,
  sent_at          timestamptz,
  created_at       timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

COMMENT ON TABLE public.ai_drafts IS
  'AI-generated message drafts awaiting human approval. '
  'Never transitions directly to sent without approved intermediate state. '
  'application_level_invariant: APPROVED before SENT — tested in Luna.';

ALTER TABLE public.ai_drafts ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

-- Studio members (owner/admin/artist) can read drafts for their studio
CREATE POLICY ai_drafts_select
  ON public.ai_drafts
  FOR SELECT
  USING (
    studio_id IN (
      SELECT sm.studio_id FROM public.studio_members sm
      WHERE sm.user_id = auth.uid()
    )
  );

-- Owner/admin/artist can UPDATE status (approve/discard)
CREATE POLICY ai_drafts_update
  ON public.ai_drafts
  FOR UPDATE
  USING (
    studio_id IN (
      SELECT sm.studio_id FROM public.studio_members sm
      WHERE sm.user_id = auth.uid()
        AND sm.role IN ('owner', 'admin', 'artist')
    )
  );

-- INSERT by service_role only (workers write the draft)
-- No DELETE policy from app

-- Indexes
CREATE INDEX idx_ai_drafts_studio_created
  ON public.ai_drafts (studio_id, created_at DESC);

CREATE INDEX idx_ai_drafts_conversation
  ON public.ai_drafts (conversation_id)
  WHERE conversation_id IS NOT NULL;

CREATE INDEX idx_ai_drafts_job
  ON public.ai_drafts (job_id);

CREATE INDEX idx_ai_drafts_pending
  ON public.ai_drafts (status)
  WHERE status = 'pending';

-- ============================================================
-- Migration: 20260514100200_ai_jobs_budget_rpc
-- Purpose  : Budget query RPC (authenticated, read-only) and
--            cost recording RPC (service_role only).
-- RPCs     :
--   get_studio_ai_budget_usage(p_studio_id uuid, p_days int DEFAULT 1)
--     → jsonb { total_cost_cents, cap_cents, budget_remaining_cents, days, job_count }
--   record_ai_cost(p_studio_id, p_job_id, p_job_type, p_model,
--                  p_input_tokens, p_output_tokens, p_cost_cents)
--     → void (service_role only)
-- Rollback :
--   DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS public.get_studio_ai_budget_usage(uuid, int);
--   DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS public.record_ai_cost(uuid, uuid, text, text, int, int, int);
-- ============================================================

-- ── A. get_studio_ai_budget_usage ────────────────────────────────────────────
-- Cap: $5/day × p_days = 500 cents × p_days
-- Authenticated studio members may call this to see their own studio's usage.
-- RLS guard inside: studio_id must be in caller's studio_members rows.

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.get_studio_ai_budget_usage(
  p_studio_id uuid,
  p_days      int DEFAULT 1
)
RETURNS jsonb
LANGUAGE plpgsql
SECURITY DEFINER
SET search_path = public
AS $$
DECLARE
  v_total_cost  bigint;
  v_job_count   bigint;
  v_cap         bigint;
  v_remaining   bigint;
BEGIN
  -- Caller must be a member of this studio
  IF NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM public.studio_members sm
    WHERE sm.studio_id = p_studio_id
      AND sm.user_id   = auth.uid()
  ) THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'Unauthorized' USING ERRCODE = '42501';
  END IF;

  SELECT
    COALESCE(SUM(ac.cost_cents), 0),
    COUNT(*)
  INTO v_total_cost, v_job_count
  FROM public.ai_costs ac
  WHERE ac.studio_id  = p_studio_id
    AND ac.created_at >= now() - (p_days || ' days')::interval;

  v_cap       := 500 * p_days;  -- $5/day in cents
  v_remaining := GREATEST(v_cap - v_total_cost, 0);

  RETURN jsonb_build_object(
    'total_cost_cents',         v_total_cost,
    'cap_cents',                v_cap,
    'budget_remaining_cents',   v_remaining,
    'days',                     p_days,
    'job_count',                v_job_count
  );
END;
$$;

-- Authenticated users may call — RLS guard inside the function
GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.get_studio_ai_budget_usage(uuid, int) TO authenticated;
REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.get_studio_ai_budget_usage(uuid, int) FROM anon;


-- ── B. record_ai_cost ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- Called by BullMQ workers (service_role) after a job completes.
-- Also updates the parent ai_jobs row (cost_cents, input_tokens, output_tokens,
-- status → done, completed_at) atomically.
-- REVOKED from authenticated to prevent app code from forging cost records.

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.record_ai_cost(
  p_studio_id     uuid,
  p_job_id        uuid,
  p_job_type      text,
  p_model         text,
  p_input_tokens  integer,
  p_output_tokens integer,
  p_cost_cents    integer
)
RETURNS void
LANGUAGE plpgsql
SECURITY DEFINER
SET search_path = public
AS $$
BEGIN
  -- Insert into cost ledger
  INSERT INTO public.ai_costs (
    studio_id,
    job_id,
    job_type,
    model,
    input_tokens,
    output_tokens,
    cost_cents
  ) VALUES (
    p_studio_id,
    p_job_id,
    p_job_type,
    p_model,
    p_input_tokens,
    p_output_tokens,
    p_cost_cents
  );

  -- Sync cost + token counts back onto the job row
  UPDATE public.ai_jobs
  SET
    cost_cents    = p_cost_cents,
    input_tokens  = p_input_tokens,
    output_tokens = p_output_tokens,
    status        = 'done',
    completed_at  = now()
  WHERE id = p_job_id;
END;
$$;

-- service_role only — revoke from all other roles
REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.record_ai_cost(uuid, uuid, text, text, integer, integer, integer) FROM PUBLIC;
REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.record_ai_cost(uuid, uuid, text, text, integer, integer, integer) FROM authenticated;
REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.record_ai_cost(uuid, uuid, text, text, integer, integer, integer) FROM anon;
-- service_role inherits superuser-equivalent, so explicit grant not required.
-- Documented here for clarity:
-- GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.record_ai_cost(...) TO service_role;
